findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders this job does not own
findings.body: The new deleteMany branch matches every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 and does not require method SMS, scheduled false, or any scheduledDate bound. WorkflowReminder also stores EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows, and an SMS row can already be scheduled true with a Twilio referenceId if a later attempt succeeds or a concurrent run records success while another run has already bumped retryCount past 1. The next cron then deletes those rows. Email and WhatsApp reminders are dropped and never send. A scheduled SMS loses its referenceId without cancelling the provider message, so the text can still go out and can no longer be tracked or cancelled. The original delete was limited to SMS; that limit was not applied to this OR branch. Scope it to unscheduled SMS rows this job actually failed.

findings.title: Broad catch burns the two-strike limit and can duplicate SMS
findings.body: The catch surrounds template building, the organizer profile lookup, getBookerBaseUrl, twilio.scheduleSMS, and the success update that sets scheduled and referenceId. Any throw increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. If Twilio already accepted the message and only the following update failed, the SID is discarded and the next cron calls scheduleSMS again, sending a duplicate; after two such errors retryCount is 2 and the opening deleteMany removes the row while those provider messages stay queued. The same path treats transient failures (DB blip, booker URL, empty attendees) as permanent send failures. This cron loads every unscheduled SMS in the next 7 days, so two errored passes delete that whole backlog and those bookings never get an SMS. Only count a retry when the provider rejects the send, and if scheduleSMS already returned a SID, persist that SID instead of incrementing.

findings.title: Missing number or empty body is retried until the send date
findings.body: retryCount is incremented only when message is non-empty and sendTo is set, and only if scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If the step has no sendTo, the booking has no smsReminderNumber, or the rendered body is empty, the loop just continues. The row stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the unbounded reschedule this PR is meant to stop (invalid or missing phone). Treat a missing destination or empty message as a terminal failure so those reminders are not loaded until the event date.

findings.title: retryCount write is not atomic under overlapping crons
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1 (here and in the catch at line 195) instead of an atomic increment. The handler loops every due reminder with several queries and a Twilio call, and it is a cron POST that can be invoked again if the previous run is still going or the scheduler retries a timeout. Two runs read the same count, both can call scheduleSMS for the same unscheduled row, and both write the same retryCount, so the retryCount > 1 delete never observes the real number of attempts and does not stop duplicate sends. Use retryCount: { increment: 1 } and claim the row before calling Twilio so a second run cannot schedule it again.

findings.title: retryCount delete is not covered by an index
findings.body: deleteMany now ORs retryCount > 1 onto the cleanup, but WorkflowReminder only indexes (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), (bookingUid), (workflowStepId), (seatReferenceId), and (cancelled, scheduledDate). The new column in schema.prisma has no index. Postgres cannot serve that OR branch from the existing composite index, so every cron run can sequentially scan WorkflowReminder before any SMS is scheduled. That table grows with bookings; a slow cleanup makes this endpoint more likely to overlap the next cron tick.

findings.title: No tests for the retry limit or what gets deleted
findings.body: This change deletes reminder rows and stops SMS after a small number of failures, and nothing in the PR covers that contract. Needed cases: one failure leaves the row and a second failure makes the next run delete it; the gt: 1 cutoff matches "failed twice" and does not allow a third scheduleSMS call; EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows with any retryCount are not deleted; a falsy scheduleSMS result and a thrown provider error both increment; empty sendTo or an empty body does not get reselected until the date; a successful schedule does not increment and is not deleted while still in the future. Without those, the unscoped OR and the two-strike catch can drop or duplicate reminders unnoticed.

findings.title: Cleanup comment no longer describes the delete
findings.body: The comment says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose scheduled date is already past. The query never filters on scheduled true, and the new OR branch also deletes any method's reminder with retryCount > 1, including future rows. Someone editing this later from the comment can restore or narrow the wrong predicate and either resurrect the infinite retry or keep deleting email and WhatsApp reminders.
